title: Cross-tenant KV cache coherence window triggers tail GPU OOMs; runtime backstop and patch
creator: Daniel Park
description:
Summary:
A cluster of production escalations across Hosted and Dedicated pools surfaced a correlated class of tail OOMs during bursty multi-tenant workloads. Symptoms: intermittent single-request spikes that drove GPU memory above reservation and caused per-node OOM kills (~2–6 events/day across affected pools). Root cause analysis indicates a coherence window in the KV cache metadata compactor combined with the CUDA allocator's deferred free behavior and slab reuse between tenants. During heavy concurrent compaction + session handoff, stale KV handle references could be observed briefly; subsequent large prefix allocations attempted to reuse partially reclaimed slabs which led to large transient allocations and failure to reclaim in time — resulting in GPU OOMs and cascading session evictions.

What makes this different from prior incidents:
- This is a cross-tenant timing/race (not simple leak): two independent subsystems (kv metadata compactor and the GPU allocator free path) expose a narrow timing window where pointers look valid but point into a slab scheduled for reuse.
- The failure manifests as bursty tail OOMs rather than steady-state leaks; customers saw spikes during traffic bursts and canary rollouts.
- Affected both Hosted and Dedicated pools; Private installs reported analogous events but only after enabling automatic session pooling.

Investigation notes and telemetry evidence:
- Correlated traces between runtime/tracing and GPU OOM logs show compaction events at T and OOM at T+10–40ms.
- Heap snapshots from debug builds show handle refcount hit 0 but metadata 'epoch' remained stale until compactor checkpoint.
- We saw session handoff traces with 'reuse_slab' flag set where the owner tenant id mismatched the active session tenant for ~30ms windows.
- Repro on a synthetic stress rig: 64 tenants, 8 concurrent compaction threads, simulated burst of long-context prefix generation reproduced OOMs 9/10 runs.

Root cause (technical):
- KV compactor moved tombstoned index slots and reclaimed slab ranges without advancing the per-handle epoch fast enough when compaction occurred concurrently with session handoff.
- CUDA allocator's deferred free + internal caching kept pointers live in the GPU allocator for tens of milliseconds, which interacted badly with slab reuse semantics and produced momentary double-ownership of slab ranges.
- No single subsystem had a full guard: compactor assumed free==safe, allocator assumed host-side refcounts were authoritative. The race allowed a transient use-after-free at slab granularity that triggered a burst allocation path to request far more memory than available.

Short-term mitigations applied (hotfix rollout):
1) Immediate mitigation (hosted and dedicated): enabled runtime oom-backstop policy v1 (preemptive soft-evict on hotspot tenants + per-tenant soft-reserve of 5% GPU memory) to dampen spikes. Deployed to hosted hot-zone within 3 hours; dedicated customers rolled via blue/green to avoid disruption.
2) Turned on extra compactor barriers: compactor now marks candidate slots as "quarantine" for 100ms before reuse to avoid immediate handoff races (configurable; default 100ms). This reduced reproducibility to 1/100 runs in stress rig.
3) Emergency dashboard and alert: created kvcache-coherence-alert (PagerDuty) and a spike dashboard (tokens/sec, compactor ops, per-tenant memory delta) to detect reoccurrence.

Permanent fix (runtime patch in flight):
- Implement epoch-based handle invalidation: each KV handle now carries a compact 16-bit epoch that must match the slab owner epoch; compactor increments epoch when reclaiming ranges. This removes the narrow timing window by making stale handles fail fast during allocation attempts. Implementation in branch: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/9842 (PR linked).
- Add allocator fallback path: when allocation sees mismatched epochs or quarantine flags, it will try a slower but safe allocator that performs synchronous device free and verification before reusing slabs. This path prevents a large burst from escalating into an OOM.
- Integrate a preemptive slab-reclamation inspector that runs during high-util windows to avoid large contiguous slab reuse without explicit handover handshake.

Rollout plan for the patch:
- Canary: runtime-1.20.3-canary on 3 hosted zones + 2 dedicated dev pools for 48 hours with the stress harness running.
- Metrics gating: no increase in request latency >5%, no OOM events for 48h, compaction ops successful rate >99.9%.
- Gradual ramp: 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% over 96h if gates pass.
- Private customer plan: a packaged runtime artifact and small preamble script to toggle quarantine window and soft-reserve; guidance doc + migration precheck.

Rollback strategy:
- If tail latency regresses or unexpected memory regressions appear, revert to quarantine + soft-reserve hotfix configuration and re-run experiments. Runtime build has fail-open flag runtime.coherence_backstop=false to disable epoch checks without restarting the control plane.

Testing & validation:
- Added deterministic chaos test that simulates compactor/allocator concurrency with deterministic scheduling to catch epoch mismatch windows. Test lives in test/chaos/kv_epoch_repro.test and added to nightly regression.
- Stress rig: 2000-run full stress with new patch shows 0 reproductions versus 9/10 before.
- Unit tests for epoch incrementing, quarantine behavior, and fallback allocator included.

Customer communications and ops playbook:
- Initial customer notification for customers affected was sent on 2025-02-13 with mitigations and ETA for permanent fix.
- Support playbook: steps to flip soft-reserve, enable quarantine window, collect heap snapshots, and apply patch. Playbook doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runtime/kvcache-coherence-2025 (internal).
- Postmortem draft started: links to incident timeline and lessons learned included.

Follow-ups (post-release):
- Post-deploy observability: add per-tenant slab churn metric and integrate with console cost/latency breakdowns.
- Long-term: consider redesigning compactor to use explicit handoff handshake between owners to eliminate quarantine tuning parameter.
- Runbook update: embed a quick 'oom-backstop' toggle in the console for SRE on-call for faster mitigation.
